subject: Reserved-lane sizing: streaming latency acceptance & GPU shortlist
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@lucidhealth.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya@lucidhealth.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — reserved-lane sizing & next technical checks

Hi Evan & Priya,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the specificity on streaming expectations. I promised to capture the follow-ups so we have a clear runbook for validating the Dedicated/reserved lanes for LucidHealth. High level summary below (short & actionable):

1) Target SLOs you confirmed on the call
   - P95 tail latency: streaming token step <= 75ms for 256-token windows (single-turn streaming).
   - Sustained throughput target: 1,200 streaming requests/minute (avg) with bursts to 3,000 RPM for 10m windows.
   - Concurrency: expect 180 active concurrent websocket streams during peak.

2) Candidate GPUs we should test (we'll produce run results):
   - NVIDIA H100 80GB (bfloat/FP16, optimal for 8k models)
   - NVIDIA A100 80GB (FP16, proven throughput for batching-heavy workloads)
   - NVIDIA L40s (cost-optimized; evaluate streaming jitter under KV-cache pressure)

3) Validation plan (technical):
   - Redwood runs model-aware streaming bench that reproduces your request-size distribution (avg 320 tokens / session; 10% 2k token sessions).
   - Bench steps: cold-start burst tests, steady-state sustained throughput, and long-lived KV-cache retention test (90m).
   - Measure: per-token latency distribution, tail latencies per connection, GPU utilization, memory pressure, and effective tokens/sec.

4) Data & artifacts you will provide
   - Sample request distribution (counts by token-length bucket) + example prompts (Priya — can you share?).
   - Permit Redwood to run a sandboxed pilot against anonymized traffic or replay (Amit, see ops note).

5) Contract/ops asks
   - We will propose a 14-day reserved pilot (committed reserved lane) to validate the SLOs with agreed exit criteria.
   - If pilot passes, we translate to a 3-month Reserved commitment with autoscale headroom.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Priya — upload sample request buckets and 5 representative prompts to the Drive folder we shared (ETA Tue, 8/31).
- Redwood (Soojin & engineering) — deliver GPU shortlist bench results + runbook (ETA Wed, 9/2).
- Ben — will scope commercial pilot terms & send a draft mutual action plan (ETA Mon, 8/31).

Attachments: throughput-bench-20260828.xlsx (initial synthetic distribution used during demo), redwood-pilot-playbook-20260828.pdf (pilot template).

If anything above is off, flag it and we'll correct. Otherwise we'll start the bench the week of 8/31 as discussed.

Thanks,
Sofia

Sofia — thanks for the write-up, this aligns with our internal expectations. A few clarifications: 

- The P95 target is an internal customer requirement for conversational UX; however, we can relax to 100ms p95 if the model variant offers better semantic quality. We'll treat 75ms as strong preference.
- For concurrency: the 180 active streams number came from peak-day traffic + warm internal users. We can provide a 24-hour sample to validate the distribution.

Priya will upload the request buckets by EOD Tue. Amit — we're good with a sandboxed traffic replay as long as PHI is scrubbed (we'll produce a scrubbed log).

One ask for Redwood: in the bench report please include a short section that explains tradeoffs between batching for cost-efficiency vs. tail-latency jitter for real-time streams. That will help our infra team sign off.

We'll await Ben's commercial terms in parallel.

Thanks,
Evan

Subject: RE: Post-demo recap — reserved-lane sizing & next technical checks

Thanks Evan — noted on the 75ms vs 100ms p95 tradeoff. A couple of technical commitments and clarifications from our side: 

Bench commitments
- We'll run the bench across the three GPU types listed (H100, A100, L40s) using the exact token-length buckets you provide. Bench will include:
  * Cold-start burst: 0 -> 3k RPM over 60s window
  * Sustained steady-state: 1,200 RPM for 60m
  * Long-lived sessions: 90m KV-cache retention with intermittent long-turn 2k-token sessions (10% of traffic)

Technical notes on tradeoffs (short):
- Batching increases aggregate throughput but adds queuing latency; for streaming we bias towards micro-batching + immediate flush for the first token and 40–80ms batching window for subsequent tokens where acceptable.
- KV cache improves latency on multi-turn dialogs but consumes GPU memory; on H100 the working set for our 8k model stays comfortably < 40GB with 75% cache hit assumptions. On L40s we expect higher eviction rates and occasional jitter.
- Quantization: INT8/4-bit quantized profiles reduce memory use (and cost) but can increase decode latency slightly on certain kernels; we'll include both FP16 and quantized runs.

Deliverables (what you'll get):
- Per-GPU tabulated results (p50/p95/p99 per-token), GPU utilization, and recommended reserved throughput headroom.
- A short runbook describing how to configure reserved lanes (burst policies, autoscale windows, fallback model variants).

Attachments: I've attached the initial bench sheet and the pilot playbook to this thread. We'll upload full raw results to the Drive link after the runs.

Next: Sofia & Ben will coordinate scheduling; we expect to start benching 9/1 AM PT if Priya uploads the sample by Tue EOD.

Regards,
